summary: Hardens identifier and literal escaping against injection: backslash escaping in eight SQL dialects and in the unknown-product ANSI fallback (with a system property to restore legacy behavior), and identifier allowlists or quoting in the Geode, Elasticsearch, MongoDB, Cassandra, and Splunk adapters.

tests.evidence: Many new unit tests; mihaibudiu asked why SplunkPushDownRuleTest uses reflection (method made package-private) and found a Cassandra test comment vague. Elasticsearch and Mongo tests exercise helpers directly, not the generated request through ElasticsearchProject/MongoAggregate.

user_docs.evidence: New system property; history.md gets an entry, but security_threat_model.md, which lists the other operator-set properties, is not updated, and the Geode/Splunk/Elasticsearch push-down behavior changes are not mentioned.

doc_comments.evidence: mihaibudiu asked for several Javadoc fixes: the Elasticsearch helper's Javadoc talks about JSON (renamed to escapeJsonString), explain possessive quantifiers, state the script language (Painless/Groovy), GeodeUtils Javadoc should not name callers, and a Cassandra comment was on the wrong line.

change_description.evidence: Deliberately generic title for a security hardening; the body lists the affected dialects and adapters and the history.md entry covers the default change.

performance.evidence: Regex matching per identifier during planning; possessive quantifiers already avoid backtracking.

security.evidence: The purpose of the change is preventing SQL/OQL/SPL/JSON/Painless injection through quoting and escaping; every escaping routine and allowlist regex (including ReDoS-safe possessive quantifiers) needs a focused security pass.

backward_compat.evidence: Changes the default of the unknown-product fallback dialect to double backslashes (new property calcite.sql.dialect.unknown.escapes.backslash, default true) and changes the literals emitted for Hive, Spark, Snowflake, Netezza, and others; on a standard-lexing backend a value containing a backslash is now a different value, not 'at worst rendered verbatim' as the Javadoc claims.

error_model.evidence: New error paths with inconsistent types: GeodeUtils.checkSafeOqlIdentifier throws bare RuntimeException, GeodeTable.checkOql throws IllegalArgumentException, GeodeRules throws IllegalArgumentException, where refusing pushdown would avoid a user-visible failure.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial escaping logic across many dialects; Netezza's own comment says backslash escapes apply only when standard-conforming-strings is off, yet the override doubles unconditionally; the Hive/Spark TRIM regex test changed expected output, which mihaibudiu called 'very complicated'.

user_value.evidence: Security hardening; the value is clear, only the opt-out property's usefulness is worth a glance.

surprising_behavior.evidence: Existing deployments on an unrecognized JDBC product silently get different string literals; Geode queries with non-identifier aliases now throw at implement time rather than falling back to Calcite evaluation, unlike Splunk and the Geode rules which refuse pushdown.

contradictions.evidence: ElasticsearchRulesTest still says callers route through escapeSpecialSymbols, a name this PR removed; GeodeTable's comment says unsafe names 'refuse pushdown' while GeodeTable/GeodeAggregate/GeodeProject throw; Geode gets three overlapping identifier regexes (GeodeUtils, GeodeTable, GeodeRules) that disagree on shape and exception type.

observability.evidence: Refused pushdowns (Splunk, Geode rules) fall back silently with no debug log; minor.

spec_conformance.evidence: Each dialect override encodes the target database's lexical rules; the reviewer said he did not verify the rules per dialect, and Netezza's and Snowflake's rules depend on session settings the dialect ignores.

plan.why: Large multi-module change: escaping logic per dialect, user-facing compatibility of the new default and throws, and test/comment consistency are separable passes.
